maria (support): seeing a sudden spike of 504s for hosted inference from us-west-2 since ~13:40 UTC, multiple customers complaining streaming sessions time out :grimacing:
maria (support): example request id req_8b4f, tenant acme-inc — hits edge gateway -> envoy -> midproxy -> model-host pool
maria (support): attaching quick curl repro I used: `curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -d @payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/stream`
tom (eng-sre): saw same in graphs, ingress h2 streams dropping and upstreams returning RST_STREAM then 504 for clients :thinking:
lee (obs): traces show fanout to 3 upstreams, two of them returned 502 with message `worker timed out` and one stayed open then sent GOAWAY
lee (obs): sampling logs: `envoy upstream reset: connection failure (reset) to 10.12.4.21:443`
sahil (infra): any recent deploys? deploy-bot: canary auth-rotation rolled 13:35 UTC to us-west-2 (canary 5%)
maria (support): customer says it started ~5m after that deploy
tom (eng-sre): plausible. auth-rotation spawns new auth-proxy pods -> increased connection churn and keepalive pool pressure
sahil (infra): checking connpool metrics — keepalive utilization shot to 98% at 13:38, new connections queued, downstream started getting 504s
sahil (infra): also seeing upstream nginx workers hitting accept queue backlog: `accept4: Resource temporarily unavailable` in syslog
lee (obs): running quick query: percentage of requests going to midproxy A increased due to weighted routing after canary -> that pod has elevated CPU and many slow open streams
lee (obs): adding this trace snippet: `span: edge.proxy -> midproxy.A -> model-hoster (long wait) -> error 502: upstream write timeout`
tom (eng-sre): immediate mitigation suggestions: 1) reduce canary to 0% (rollback) 2) bump keepalive pool size on edge proxy 3) throttle session concurrency for affected tenants
maria (support): customer-ops, want me to enable tenant-level throttle for acme-inc now?
customer-ops: yes please, set concurrency to 3 and enable short backoff for streaming calls
sahil (infra): applied tenant throttle via runtime config: `tenants.acme.concurrency=3` — watching
sahil (infra): also increased edge proxy keepalive pools + tune `http2.max_concurrent_streams` on midproxy
lee (obs): after throttle + pool bump, 504s dropped to baseline within ~90s. graphs show healthy SLOs again
maria (support): customer confirmed streams resumed and tokens continued to be billed correctly, thank you :relieved:
tom (eng-sre): root cause hypothesis: canary auth rotation changed routing weights and briefly focused traffic on a midproxy instance with insufficient worker capacity causing accept queue backpressure -> envoys reset/upstream 502 -> client 504s
tom (eng-sre): follow-ups: 1) add preflight load check in canary rollout to detect accept-queue/backpressure 2) add autoscaling threshold on midproxy based on h2-streams + accept queue 3) improve healthcheck to consider accept queue depth
sahil (infra): I'll open infra ticket and link infra-runbook for keepalive tuning
sahil (infra): ticket INF-2028 created: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2028
maria (support): filing support RCA to share with customers, tagging stakeholders
maria (support): short timeline + actions in case notes: rollback canary, tenant throttle, bump pools, ticket INF-2028
tom (eng-sre): nice triage. leaving follow-up to infra/obs. :thumbsup:
